config.title: Multi-Step Form

intro.title: Multi-Step Form
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a multi-step form using Vue, which allows users to progress through a form in stages, like a sign-up or checkout process. You will learn how to manage the current step state and conditionally display different form sections based on that state. The main technologies involved are Vue's reactive data properties, conditional rendering with v-if or v-show, and event handling for navigation buttons. By the end, you'll have a functional form that guides users through multiple steps with clear navigation.
intro.usecase: Multi-step forms are essential in real-world applications where complex data collection needs to be broken down into manageable sections. You'll see this pattern in e-commerce checkout flows, user onboarding processes, insurance quote calculators, and job application platforms. As a Vue developer, you'll implement these interfaces to guide users through sequential tasks while maintaining application state between steps. This approach improves user experience by reducing cognitive load and preventing form abandonment during lengthy data entry processes.

objectives: Construct a multi-step form component with separate sections for each step
Initialize and manage reactive state to track the current step and form data
Implement navigation handlers to control progression between form steps
Bind form inputs to reactive data properties using v-model
Configure conditional rendering to display only the active step
Integrate validation logic to enable/disable navigation buttons
Render a visual progress indicator that updates with step changes

steps.title: Import Vue and ref
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from the 'vue' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a module
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue and ref from 'vue' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref function are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create and export a default Vue component named MultiStepForm with a setup function that returns an empty template.
steps.hint: Use the Vue defineComponent function to create the component structure. The setup function should return an empty object for now.
steps.seedCode:
import { defineComponent } from 'vue';

// Create and export a default Vue component named MultiStepForm with a setup function that returns an empty template.
steps.expectedOutcome: A MultiStepForm component is defined with a setup function that returns an empty object.
successCriteria: The component is named MultiStepForm, uses defineComponent, has a setup function, and returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using defineComponent, naming the component MultiStepForm, and the setup function returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a Vue component using defineComponent with the name MultiStepForm and a setup function that returns an empty object.

steps.title: Initialize current step state
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, use ref to create a reactive variable named currentStep and initialize it to 1.
steps.hint: Remember to call ref() with the initial value 1 and assign it to a variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating reactive state
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has reactive state to track which step of the form is currently active.
successCriteria: A currentStep variable is declared using ref and initialized to 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref() and initializing currentStep to 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a reactive variable named currentStep initialized to 1 using ref.

steps.title: Create next step handler
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a function named nextStep that increments currentStep by 1, but only if currentStep is less than 3 (since we'll have 3 steps total).
steps.hint: You can define a function inside setup using regular function syntax or arrow function. Use an if statement to check if currentStep.value is less than 3 before incrementing it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A nextStep function is defined that conditionally increments currentStep when called.
successCriteria: The nextStep function is defined, checks if currentStep.value < 3, and increments currentStep.value by 1 when the condition is true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it checks if currentStep.value is less than 3 before incrementing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The nextStep function isn't defined correctly. Create a function that increments currentStep only when it's less than 3.

steps.title: Create previous step handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named prevStep that decrements the currentStep value by 1, but only if currentStep is greater than 1.
steps.hint: Inside the setup function, define a function that checks if currentStep.value > 1 before decreasing it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A prevStep function is defined that safely moves to the previous step when possible.
successCriteria: The prevStep function is defined, checks that currentStep > 1, and decrements currentStep.value by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a prevStep function, but make sure it includes the condition to check if currentStep is greater than 1 before decrementing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The prevStep function is missing or doesn't properly handle moving to the previous step. Try creating a function that checks if currentStep > 1 before decreasing it.

steps.title: Add step indicator markup
steps.instruction: Inside the component's setup return object, add a div element with class 'step-indicator' that displays the current step number and total steps (e.g., 'Step 1 of 3').
steps.hint: Use template literals with currentStep.value to show the current step. You can hardcode the total steps as 3 for now.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: step indicator markup
Step 1 of 3
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a div with class 'step-indicator' showing the current step number and total steps.
successCriteria: The return object includes a div element with class 'step-indicator' that displays text like 'Step 1 of 3'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the div has class 'step-indicator' and displays the current step number and total steps.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step indicator markup is missing or incorrect. Add a div with class 'step-indicator' showing the current step and total steps.

steps.title: Create step 1 form fields
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function's return object, add two input fields for step 1: one for name and one for email. Use v-model to bind each input to the corresponding property in formData.
steps.hint: Add <input> elements with v-model directives like v-model="formData.name" and v-model="formData.email". Place them inside the return object.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: binding input to reactive data
<input v-model="userData.username" placeholder="Enter username">
steps.expectedOutcome: The return object now includes two input fields bound to formData.name and formData.email.
successCriteria: Two input fields are present in the return object, each with v-model binding to formData properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some form fields, but make sure both name and email inputs are present and correctly bound with v-model.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step 1 form fields are missing or not properly bound. Add two input fields with v-model="formData.name" and v-model="formData.email".

steps.title: Create step 2 form fields
steps.instruction: Add a second step section with form fields for address and phone number, using v-model to bind them to the formData state.
steps.hint: Use v-model to bind input values to formData properties. Remember to wrap step 2 content in a conditional v-if or v-show.
steps.analogousExample: // Similar: form fields for step 2
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a second step with address and phone input fields bound to formData.
successCriteria: Step 2 form fields are added with v-model binding to formData properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some step 2 fields, but make sure all required fields are present and properly bound with v-model.
steps.feedbackWrong: Step 2 form fields are missing or not properly implemented. Check that you've added address and phone inputs with v-model binding.

steps.title: Add navigation buttons with event handlers
steps.instruction: Add Previous and Next buttons inside your component's template, with @click handlers that call your prevStep and nextStep functions respectively.
steps.hint: Use <button> elements with @click directives. Place them after your step 2 form fields.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your form will have Previous and Next buttons that navigate between steps when clicked.
successCriteria: Two buttons with @click handlers calling prevStep and nextStep are added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added buttons, but check that both have @click handlers calling the correct functions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation buttons are missing or not properly wired to the step handlers.
